2608.19140.title: Grouping the Stochastic Machine: Precision, Not Capability, as the Frontier Metric for AI Systems
2608.19140.paper_summary: Frontier language models are compared, marketed, and benchmarked on capability -- what their best or average output can achieve. I argue this measures the wrong axis. The models have saturated accuracy: their mean output lands on the target. What now separates one system from another in practice is precision: how tightly concentrated their outputs are around that target across repeated, identical requests. Borrowing the marksman's distinction, capability is where the average shot lands; reliability is the size of the group. I make three claims. First, precision, not capability, is the frontier differentiator between systems, and benchmark culture systematically fails to measure it, reporting central tendency rather than spread. Second, precision is measurable, cheaply and without circularity, by running a fixed suite of deterministically scored tasks many times at fixed temperature and computing the per-task consistency of outcomes -- no model-in-the-loop grader required. Third, the measurement is not merely descriptive but decision-guiding: it separates consistent failures (a tight group off-centre, correctable by the operating discipline of Paper 1 -- a sight adjustment) from scattered failures (a wide group, correctable only by changing the model or its sampling -- a rifle problem). I define a grouping metric, specify a harness, and show how tracking a human-AI pair's grouping over time yields the compounding signal that Paper 1's field study requires. A first real run, since replicated, illustrates both the method and its most important limit: one measured gap was closed completely by a single rule (0/5 -> 5/5), while a suite of tasks authored from the rules themselves found no value, because a frontier model already embodies explicit good practice -- establishing that a discipline's worth is found by measurement on real work, not constructed from its own rulebook.
2608.19140.paper_summary_zh: 前沿語言模型的比較、行銷和基準測試是基於能力——它們的最佳或平均輸出能達到什麼。我認為這測量了錯誤的軸線。這些模型的準確性已經飽和：它們的平均輸出落在目標上。現在在實踐中區分一個系統與另一個系統的因素是精確度：它們的輸出在重複、相同請求下圍繞那個目標的集中程度。借用射手的區分，能力是平均射擊落點；可靠性是群體的大小。我提出三個主張。首先，精確度，而非能力，是系統之間的前沿區分者，而基準文化系統性地未能測量它，報告的是集中趨勢而非分散度。第二，精確度是可測量的，成本低且不具循環性，可以通過在固定溫度下多次運行一組確定性評分的任務來計算每個任務的結果一致性——不需要模型內部的評分者。第三，這一測量不僅僅是描述性的，而是指導決策的：它將一致的失敗（偏心的緊密群體，可以通過《論文 1》的操作紀律進行校正——一個瞄準調整）與分散的失敗（寬鬆的群體，只能通過改變模型或其抽樣進行校正——一個步槍問題）區分開來。我定義了一個分組指標，指定了一個框架，並展示了如何追蹤人類-人工智慧配對的分組隨時間變化，產生《論文 1》的實地研究所需的累積信號。一個首次的真實運行，由於被複製，展示了這種方法及其最重要的限制：一個測量的差距完全被一條規則關閉（0/5 -> 5/5），而從這些規則本身創建的一套任務則未找到任何價值，因為前沿模型已經體現了明確的良好實踐——確立了一個學科的價值是通過對真實工作的測量來發現的，而不是從其自身的規則手冊中構建出來的。
2608.19140.author: George Andrikopoulos et.al.
